biography: Ricardo Maurício's journey began on the dusty karting tracks of São Paulo, where his raw talent was immediately apparent. Growing up idolizing Ayrton Senna, he relentlessly honed his skills, often skipping school to squeeze in extra practice laps. His aggressive style quickly earned him local notoriety, and by the age of 18, he secured a spot in the Porsche GT3 Cup Challenge Brasil. His transition to touring cars was seamless, and he quickly became a force to be reckoned with, known for his daring overtakes and unwavering determination. He has been with Eurofarma RC for a significant portion of his career, becoming synonymous with the team. Now at 33, Maurício is at the peak of his powers, a seasoned veteran with a burning desire to add more championships to his already impressive resume.
drivingStyle: Maurício is an aggressive and opportunistic driver, always searching for the slightest opening to exploit. His corner entry speed is exceptional, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. While occasionally prone to overdriving, he has developed a keen sense of tire management, knowing when to push and when to conserve. Under pressure, he remains remarkably calm, a trait that has served him well in numerous high-stakes situations. His aggressive style can come at a cost, but when it pays off, the rewards are substantial.

famousQuote: Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about taking risks and pushing boundaries. Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the Stock Car Pro Series championship in 2020 after a nail-biting final race where he overtook his main rival on the last lap, securing the title by a single point.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2015 Curitiba Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure, costing him a certain victory and severely impacting his championship chances.
